Q: How can I get an HTML element to react to :hover at a z-index under 0? A:

z-index: -1 by itself doesn't disable :hover. It only changes the element's position within its stacking context.

The important question is which element is actually receiving the pointer event. If another positioned element is painted above the dropdown, that element will be hit-tested first, so the dropdown never gets hovered. If nothing is covering it, a negative z-index can still work.

I'd verify this before changing the CSS:

  1. Open DevTools and inspect the element while moving the mouse over the area.

  2. Check whether the dropdown is actually the topmost element at that point or whether the header (or another ancestor) is covering it.

  3. Also inspect the stacking contexts created by positioned elements, transform, opacity, filter, etc., since those often produce unexpected z-index behavior.

Without seeing the full HTML/CSS it's difficult to say that z-index: -1 is the root cause. In many cases the real issue is an overlapping element or a different stacking context rather than the negative value itself.

Q: TypeScript Says Intersection Property Does Not Exist A:

TypeScript infers the type of mapped from it's first assignment (initialization), so it's IPerson[]:

In TypeScript, there are several places where type inference is used to provide type information when there is no explicit type annotation. For example, in this code

let x = 3;

The type of the x variable is inferred to be number. This kind of inference takes place when initializing variables and members, setting parameter default values, and determining function return types.

Taken from "Type inference" chapter from the TypeScript handbook (I linked it's upcoming 2.0 beta version), I recommend reading this.

The second assignment then doesn't extend the definition, but is no error either because objects can have additional properties. When you're accessing _id, you get an error because TypeScript cannot be sure from the initially inferred type that the array entries also contain _id properties.

Note: casting with mapped = collection.map(mapperB) as Array<IPerson & IWithId> gives TypeScript no additional information, so the outcome is the same.

To ease reasoning about types, I personally recommend assigning transformed values to new variables (as you proposed with const mapped2 = collection.map(mapperB). And choose expressive variable names (with tradeoff of becoming lengthy, but this shouldn't happen that often if you keep your function complexity small enough):

const filteredList = list.filter(...);
const filteredListWithIds = filteredList.map(...)

Not directly related, but an error: Array.prototype.map() returns a new array. The value of mapped from let mapped = collection.map(mapperA) is lost immediately as its being overwritten at the next line during mapped = collection.map(mapperB)`. Maybe a mistake when creating the playground example based on your real code?

Q: NoClassDefFoundError: Failed resolution of: Landroid/support/v4/os/BuildCompat; A:

I faced with this proplem .And I think problem is :

compile 'com.google.android.gms:play-services:9.8.0'

You complile with may packages .In some cases, doing so made it more difficult to keep the number of methods in your app (including framework APIs, library methods, and your own code) under the 65,536 limit . Q: selenium webdriver url navigation (on microsoft edge with window10) , hang after 28/29th url A:

You are missing Edge browser standalone server. Download it from WebDriver for Microsoft Edge, and place it in the same directory where the scripts are stored.

Try the code snippet below, working fine for me -

import os
from selenium import webdriver

# create new Edge session
dir = os.path.dirname(__file__)
edge_path = dir + "\MicrosoftWebDriver.exe"
driver = webdriver.Edge(edge_path)
driver.implicitly_wait(10)
# driver.maximize_window()

driver.get("https://www.freelancer.in/")

login_button = driver.find_element_by_class_name("LandingHeader-authBtn")
login_button.click()

Q: Prevent a label from "scrolling" when a count is being updated from a ListView control A:

In ListView, you can make a group selection or cancel it as follows:

  1. Shift + End/Home
  2. Shift + LB Mouse Click
  3. By selecting a rectangular area with the mouse
  4. By code, for example, ListView1.SelectedItems.Clear()

In any of these cases, as many ItemSelectionChanged events will occur as the items will change their state.

As far as I understood your question, you are only interested in the final state. Therefore, I suggest unsubscribing from the ItemSelectionChanged event before the group update and re-subscribing to it after.

Of course, after all these actions, Label2 will not be updated. To do this, you will need to call ListView1_ItemSelectionChanged method manually.

Since you are subscribed to the ItemSelectionChanged event again, the ListView1_ItemSelectionChanged method will be called in any cases described above.

Public Class Form1

    Private Sub ListView1_ItemSelectionChanged(sender As Object, e As ListViewItemSelectionChangedEventArgs) Handles ListView1.ItemSelectionChanged
        Label2.Text = Format(ListView1.SelectedItems.Count, "000;;#") ' pos;neg;zero
    End Sub

    Private Sub Button1_Click(sender As Object, e As EventArgs) Handles Button1.Click
        ' ********** Select All button **********
        RemoveHandler ListView1.ItemSelectionChanged, AddressOf ListView1_ItemSelectionChanged
        For Each item In ListView1.Items
            If item.Selected = False Then item.Selected = True
        Next
        AddHandler ListView1.ItemSelectionChanged, AddressOf ListView1_ItemSelectionChanged
        ListView1_ItemSelectionChanged(ListView1, Nothing)
    End Sub

    ' --

    Private Sub Button3_Click(sender As Object, e As EventArgs) Handles Button3.Click
        ' ********** Select None button **********
        RemoveHandler ListView1.ItemSelectionChanged, AddressOf ListView1_ItemSelectionChanged
        For Each item In ListView1.Items
            If item.Selected = True Then item.Selected = False
        Next
        AddHandler ListView1.ItemSelectionChanged, AddressOf ListView1_ItemSelectionChanged
        ListView1_ItemSelectionChanged(ListView1, Nothing)
    End Sub

    ' --

End Class

To avoid repeating the code in several places, I suggest wrapping the selection process in the single (DoSelect) method with the (action) delegate call inside:

Public Class Form1

    Private Sub ListView1_ItemSelectionChanged(sender As Object, e As ListViewItemSelectionChangedEventArgs) Handles ListView1.ItemSelectionChanged
        Label2.Text = Format(ListView1.SelectedItems.Count, "000;;#") ' pos;neg;zero
    End Sub

    Private Sub DoSelect(action As Action)
        RemoveHandler ListView1.ItemSelectionChanged, AddressOf ListView1_ItemSelectionChanged
        action()
        AddHandler ListView1.ItemSelectionChanged, AddressOf ListView1_ItemSelectionChanged
        ListView1_ItemSelectionChanged(ListView1, Nothing)
    End Sub

    Private Sub Button1_Click(sender As Object, e As EventArgs) Handles Button1.Click
        ' ********** Select All button **********
        DoSelect(
            Sub()
                For Each item In ListView1.Items
                    If item.Selected = False Then item.Selected = True
                Next
            End Sub)
    End Sub

    ' --

    Private Sub Button3_Click(sender As Object, e As EventArgs) Handles Button3.Click
        ' ********** Select None button **********
        DoSelect(
            Sub()
                For Each item In ListView1.Items
                    If item.Selected = True Then item.Selected = False
                Next
            End Sub)
    End Sub

    ' --

End Class
